ownerAuthorization: Let's do a batch of all unupdated cards categorized as "picture" in the suitability reivew.
scope: Review only; no activation, eligibility, audio or progress changes.

items.rationale: A child is a workable broad category in an illustration.
items.recommendation: Use a consistent named child with juvenile proportions; do not test exact age, gender or family role from appearance. Exclude overlapping child categories, including 女の子, 少年, 少女, 男の子 and 赤ちゃん, as competing picture answers.
items.currentVisualConcept: A child holding a toy pinwheel
items.currentVisualReviewNote: A child is indicated by proportions and a toy; age remains approximate.

items.rationale: A circle can be shown directly as a shape.
items.recommendation: Use a plain circle; exclude 丸い and round objects as competing answers.
items.currentVisualConcept: A simple flat pink circle

items.rationale: An eye can be depicted directly.
items.recommendation: Use an eye in a face or a clear eye close-up; never contrast with 目玉 in a picture-only question.
items.currentVisualConcept: An eye with iris and pupil

items.rationale: An eyeball has a direct anatomical referent, but overlaps eye.
items.recommendation: Use a simple anatomy view; share or exclude eye-family images rather than forcing a 目 versus 目玉 contrast.
items.currentVisualConcept: A round eyeball with iris and pupil
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Eye and eyeball should not be contrasted in a picture-only quiz.

items.rationale: A girl can be introduced through a consistent illustrated character; the two words overlap in this source gloss.
items.recommendation: Share an established girl character and exclude synonymous girl cards from distractors; teach 女子 usage/register in context, not through hair or clothes.
items.currentVisualConcept: A young girl with pigtails holding a ball
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Gender cannot be known from hairstyle; both source words intentionally share this scene.

items.rationale: A recognizable convenience-store storefront and stocked small-shop interior can establish the concrete place.

items.rationale: A varied group of meat cuts directly represents the category.

items.rationale: An enlarged skin or outer-covering sample can depict a concrete intended sense.
items.recommendation: Teach one sense clearly, such as skin, hide or peel; avoid implying a human skin cross-section exhausts the word's scope. Its reading かわ also matches 川 in level 1; require context if those meanings compete.
items.currentVisualConcept: Magnified layered skin patch with pores and hair.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Educational skin cross-section; 皮 can also refer to other coverings.

items.rationale: A clear educational anatomical illustration can identify the body part directly.
items.recommendation: Use an accurate simple anatomical cutaway and teach that the Japanese word is colloquial; no sexualized presentation is needed.
items.currentVisualConcept: Simple educational diagram shows paired testes in a neutral anatomical cutaway.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Tasteful nonsexual simplified educational anatomy; verify anatomical clarity and suitability for the owner’s lesson bank.

items.rationale: A clear dynamic running pose is a recognizable action.
items.recommendation: Keep bent arms, stride and motion cues readable; use context for vehicles or figurative senses later.
items.currentVisualConcept: Runner leans forward with bent arms and long strides.
